key_insight: A small independent checker converts admissible potential and exactly charge-conserving current fields into guaranteed error bounds for PDE outputs from conventional solvers, LLM-written code, and neural surrogates.
engineering_relevance: Physics-based certificates can expose incorrect simulation results that pass grid-convergence studies, helping engineers audit automated computational pipelines.
method: Require each solver to provide a potential–current certificate.
Check admissibility and exact charge conservation against a written physics specification.
Compute guaranteed per-output error bounds, including for reduced-basis neural predictions.
evidence_signal: The checker rejected or refuted all five convergent buggy solvers; reduced-basis neural predictions received bounds at most 0.0021% wide in-range and 0.3–25% wide out-of-range, where 90% conformal intervals covered none of 14 tests.
watch_item: Guarantees apply only to the stated model; informative bounds require energy-accurate outputs on a resolving grid, and free-nodal neural outputs produced valid but uninformative bounds.
paper_title: Verifying the Outputs of PDE Solvers: From Finite Elements to Neural Surrogates
